Subject: Cabana POC - ask to extend + quick pricing question

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from our side — the engineering team is asking for an extra 3 weeks on the POC to validate latency under a realistic production load. We have two constraints: procurement wants a single invoice this quarter, and our exec sponsor wants a clearer SLA commitment if we extend.

Can you outline what options Redwood has for extending the timebox? Specifically: a) a one-time acceleration/extension fee we can invoice this quarter, or b) a bridging credit model (prepaid credits applied to usage) which would avoid pro forma invoicing but might be harder for our finance team to track.

Also: we’ll need priority engineering time for the first week of the extension (about 12 hours) and a written fallback if the new SLA target isn’t met.

Appreciate a short options list I can take back to procurement.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Rivers
Head of Product, Cabana.ai

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Two pragmatic paths we commonly use; I’ll summarize pros/cons and a recommended blended approach below so procurement can decide quickly. I attached a short quote showing the math (Redwood-Pilot-RevB-Quote.pdf).

Option A — Acceleration fee (one-time invoice)
- Scope: +3 weeks timebox, includes priority infra scheduling and 16 engineering hours (onsite remote support) during the extension window.
- Cost: one-time fee $24,000 (invoice this quarter).
- SLA: we’ll commit to a 99.5% inference availability target for the extension window; if we miss by >0.5% we credit 10% of the fee.
- Pros: matches procurement requirement for a single invoice; simple bookkeeping.
- Cons: immediate cash outlay, no credits toward longer-term committed usage.

Option B — Bridging credits (prepaid usage credit)
- Scope: 60k token credit bucket to cover the extended load + 12 engineering hours priority.
- Cost: $20,000 in credits (prepaid). Net effective discount: 15% vs list generation rates.
- SLA: credits do not change runtime SLA but we’ll add a contractual response-time clause for incidents during the extension window.
- Pros: preserves cash flow classification for Cabana, credits reduce per-token cost.
- Cons: procurement may not treat as a single invoice; accounting prefers invoices.

Recommended blended path (middle-ground) — what procurement often signs quickly:
- 50% acceleration fee ($12k invoice this quarter) + 50% bridging credits ($10k applied as token credits).
- Engineering: we can commit 14 hours (split across two weeks) rather than 16 to keep overall price flat.
- SLA: 99.5% availability with a credit back (5% of acceleration portion) if missed; explicit RTO for incident response in SOW.

Next steps if this looks acceptable: 1) I’ll have Legal prepare a short addendum + SOW, 2) we’ll send a DocuSign link for the blended addendum, 3) we provision infra priority after signature.

Thoughts? If you prefer, we can kick to David to confirm commercial/legal constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
